highlighted_text.text: Elizabeth left Stanford University's School of Engineering to build Theranos around her patents and belief that access to health information is a basic human right
Theranos' breakthrough advancements have made it possible to quickly process the full range of laboratory tests from a few drops of blood - instead of numerous tubes - and at unprecedented low costs
She is the youngest person to be awarded the Horatio Alger Award, and was named one of the TIME 100 Most Influential People in the World in 2015
She has an honorary doctorate from Pepperdine University and is a board member of the Harvard Medical School Board of Fellows and the CSIS Board of Trustees
Sunny joined Theranos after dropping out of the Computer Science program at Stanford University
Previously, he held the positions of Chairman & CEO from 1996-2014, President & CEO from 1990-1996 and President & COO from 1989-1990
Dr. Foege received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012, the nation's highest civilian honor
Senator Frist represented Tennessee in the U.S. Senate for 12 years where he served on both the Health and Finance committees
Dr. Kissinger served as Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs from 1969-1975 and as Secretary of State from 1973-1977
Richard Kovacevich served as the Chief Executive Officer of Wells Fargo & Company from 1998-2007 and Chairman of the Board from 2001-2009
General Mattis retired after more than 41 years of service to the nation

facts: Elizabeth Holmes founded Theranos in 2003 after leaving Stanford University's School of Engineering.
Sunny Balwani serves as the President and Chief Operating Officer of Theranos.
Riley P. Bechtel is Chairman of the Board and a Director of Bechtel Group, Inc.
David Boies serves as the Chairman of Boies, Schiller & Flexner LLP.
William H. Foege is an epidemiologist and former director of the U.S. Center for Disease Control and Prevention.
Henry A. Kissinger served as Secretary of State from 1973 to 1977.
